paper.title: Bounded regret in stochastic multi-armed bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed case, known mu^(star) and Delta
unmapped: learner knows the optimal mean mu_star exactly (WLOG mu_star = 0)
learner knows the gap Delta exactly
settings.definition_quote: In this section we investigate a toy example where $K=2$ and the agent knows exactly both $\mu^{(\star)}=0$ (without loss of generality) and $\Delta$.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed, known mu^(star) and lower bound epsilon on smallest gap
unmapped: learner knows the optimal mean mu_star exactly (WLOG 0)
learner knows epsilon > 0 with epsilon <= Delta_min (a lower bound on the smallest gap)
settings.definition_quote: In this section we consider the general multi-armed case, when the agent knows $\mu^{(\star)}=0$ (without loss of generality) and an $\epsilon>0$ such that $\epsilon \leq \Delta$.

unmapped: learner knows the optimal mean mu_star exactly (WLOG 0)
no information on the smallest gap
settings.definition_quote: Note that we also analyze the case where $\epsilon = 0$ (that is, when we have no information on the smallest gap).

unmapped: learner knows Delta but not mu_star; hard instances: one Dirac arm at 0 and one N(+-Delta,1) arm
learner knows mu_star = 0 but not Delta; Gaussian unit-variance instances

source.label: th:alg1
source.quote: Policy~\ref{fig:alg1} has regret bounded as $R_n \leq \Delta + 16/\Delta$, uniformly in $n$.

results.notes: K=2 so Delta is the single gap.

bound.regime: epsilon in (0, min(1, Delta_min)], all n >= 1

symbols.epsilon: known lower bound on the smallest gap

source.label: th:algPsi
source.quote: Fix $\epsilon \in (0, 1 \wedge \Delta]$, then Policy~\ref{fig:alg3} associated with the potential $\psi(x)=x^2$ satisfies for all $n \geq 1$, R_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \Big\{ \Delta_i+\frac{32}{\Delta_i}\log\big(\frac{5}{\epsilon}\big) \Big\}

results.notes: epsilon used as known gap lower bound, not PAC accuracy.

symbols.v: second moment E (Y_1^(star))^2 of the optimal arm's reward

source.label: th:algPsi
source.quote: Furthermore for $\epsilon = 0$, let $v = \E \left(Y_1^{(\star)}\right)^2$, then the regret is bounded as R_n \leq \sum_{i : \Delta_i >0}  \Big\{\Delta_i + (1 \vee v)\frac{4 \log(9 n)}{\Delta_i} \Big\}

results.notes: Policy does not use n; bound holds for each n.

symbols.epsilon: known lower bound on the smallest gap

source.label: th:algPsi
source.quote: The dependency in $\epsilon$ can be reduced by using the potential $\psi(x) = \frac{x^2}{\log(4 x/\epsilon)}$ since it yields R_n \leq \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0}\Big\{ \Delta_i+\frac{32\log\big(\frac{2\Delta_i}{\varepsilon}\big)}{\Delta_i}\big[3+   \log\log\big(\frac{4}{\epsilon}\big)\big]\Big\}

extra_assumptions: Gaussian unit-variance instances N(0,1) x N(-Delta,1) and its permutation

source.label: th:LB1
source.quote:
Let $
u= \cN(0,1) \otimes \cN(- \Delta,1)$ and $
u' = \cN(-\Delta,1) \otimes \cN(0,1)$. Then for any policy, and for every $n \geq 1$, $$\max\left(R_n(
u), R_n(
u')ight) \ge  rac{1}{4\Delta}\,.$$

results.notes: Max over two instances with known gap Delta and known mu_star; theorem numbering follows shared counter (Theorem 1,2,3, Lemma 4?) — numbering uncertain.

extra_assumptions: instances delta_0 x N(-Delta,1) and delta_0 x N(Delta,1)

source.label: th:LB2
source.quote:
Let $
u= \delta_0 \otimes \cN(- \Delta,1)$ and $
u' = \delta_0 \otimes \cN(\Delta,1)$. Then for any policy, and any $n \geq 1$, $$\max\left(R_n(
u), R_n(
u')ight) \geq  rac{\log(n \Delta^2 / 2)}{4 \Delta} .$$

results.notes: Theorem number inferred from shared counter (uncertain). The two instances have different mu_star.

extra_assumptions: instances N(0,1) x N(-1,1) and N(-Delta,1) x N(0,1), Delta in (0,1], all with mu_star = 0

source.label: th:LB3
source.quote:
Let $
u_0 = \cN(0,1) \otimes \cN(-1,1)$, and $
u_{\Delta} = \cN(-\Delta,1) \otimes \cN(0,1)$, $\Delta \in (0,1]$. Then for any policy, and any $n \geq 1$, $$\max\left(R_n(
u_0), \sup_{\Delta \in (0,1]} \Delta R_n(
u_{\Delta})ight) \geq  rac{1}{2} \log(n / 139) .$$

results.notes: Quantity is gap-rescaled regret Delta*R_n (max over instances); equivalently some instance has R_n >= log(n/139)/(2 Delta). Theorem number inferred.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit without prior knowledge on distributions; asymptotic lower bound
